prompts.prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Create a refined, exceptionally legible teaching illustration for GIGAWATT, a serious course about AI data centers. Asset: a wide landscape 16:9 isometric architectural cutaway of ONE hypothetical data-center campus, on a warm ivory background (#f4f3ee), clean editorial engineering illustration with precise geometry, subtle ambient shadows, dark blue-gray equipment, restrained amber power accents, teal cooling equipment, blue communication cable accents. Show a medium-voltage electrical yard on the LEFT leading spatially to a compact electrical service room, an open-roof DATA HALL at CENTER with six clearly separated rows of dark server racks, and a MECHANICAL YARD on the RIGHT with dry cooler fan units and a distinct chiller; service pipes connect the building to that yard. No solar panels, no power station, no cooling tower, no human figures. Make component functions spatially distinguishable and service aisles plausible; do not add tangled pipes or decorative wires. Composition is a teaching model, not an actual site design: one clean building cutaway fills 80% of frame, plenty of margin, readily recognizable silhouettes at phone size, near-orthographic isometric camera. Absolutely NO text, numbers, arrows, labels, logos, brand marks, watermarks, measurement markings or glows. Labels and exact flow arrows will be added in accessible code. This should look like an elegant technical museum exhibit, not a sci-fi render or marketing hero. Every visible object should help explain where power enters, computation happens and heat exits.

Use case: scientific-educational. Create a beautifully clear landscape 16:9 teaching illustration for GIGAWATT. Show ONE hypothetical liquid-cooled AI server rack in a clean three-quarter cutaway, with ONE generic compute tray slid outward in the foreground, revealing a circuit board with four simple accelerator packages covered by copper cold plates and paired supply/return coolant tubes. The rack behind has distinct dark compute trays in its lower and upper sections, a visually distinct middle bank of networking switch trays with subtle blue cable details, a separate upper group of silver power conversion shelves, and two vertical teal coolant manifolds visible along one rear edge. Emphasize hierarchy rack -> tray -> chips by spatial composition, NOT detached floating duplicates. No specific NVIDIA product likeness or exact rack unit counts required; this is illustrative equipment anatomy, not a wiring or mechanical design. Editorial engineering illustration on warm ivory #f4f3ee, dark slate equipment, restrained amber for power hardware, teal tubes and copper cold plates, gentle ambient shadows, precise simple silhouettes, large features legible on a phone. Leave margins and clean negative space. No text, numbers, labels, arrows, logos, branding, watermarks, laser beams, smoke or glowing neon. The teaching question is: how do power, coolant and communication meet the same compute tray?

Use case: scientific-educational. Create an elegant wide 16:9 educational equipment cutaway for the GIGAWATT data-center course. A clean left-to-right spatial assembly of three recognizable equipment groups on a warm ivory #f4f3ee background: LEFT a generic server compute tray with four copper cold plates attached to accelerator packages and short paired coolant tubes; CENTER an opened coolant distribution cabinet showing a single plate heat exchanger made of stacked silver plates, two pump modules and distinct pipe connections on either side; RIGHT a simple outdoor dry cooler with two large fans over a finned heat-exchange coil. Visually distinguish the two closed liquid circuits: teal tubing between chip cold plates and one SIDE of the plate heat exchanger; muted blue tubing from the OTHER SIDE of that exchanger to the outdoor cooler. The two fluids NEVER mix and never cross through the plate stack as one continuous pipe. Each circuit has two separate pipes, supply and return, for a physically interpretable loop. No extra plant, no chiller, no tower, no tanks, no floating droplets. Oblique near-isometric camera, visually simplified cutaway suitable for teaching equipment roles, not a buildable piping design. Refined technical museum illustration, dark slate housings, copper cold plates, subtle realistic surfaces, ample margins. Absolutely no text, no arrows, no numbers, no logos or watermark. Exact process directions and physical equations will be drawn in code outside this illustration.
